title: FDA-authorized AI devices
line: filterable registry of every AI device the FDA has authorized
question: What does the FDA's public list of AI-enabled devices record, and what does it leave out about whether those devices help patients?
data: FDA AI-Enabled Medical Devices list (pulled 30 Mar 2026)
calls: per-device table and aggregate evidence findings kept in separate sections. the published studies report across the whole list, so no single device can carry one of those values.
framed as an evidence and transparency question, not as 510(k) clearance being wrongdoing. the pathway is legal and often appropriate.
missing fields reported as not reported, not as not done. a study may exist and simply be absent from the public summary, which is itself the finding.
says plainly that the list undercounts. it is assembled from AI terminology in public summaries, so devices can be missing.
broke: v1 was a fixed essay whose headline figures came from an older snapshot and secondary sources of different vintages.
the page's own copy read as machine-written on a later teardown: adversative title, hero stats, closing aphorism. rewritten against my style rules.
tried: v1 was a static evidence essay built on other people's summary figures. rebuilt as a filterable registry over the FDA's own downloaded list, so the per-device record and the aggregate evidence stay visibly separate.
